title: OpenStax Calculus Volume 3, 6.2 Line Integrals: Calculate a scalar line integral along a curve.
summary: OpenStax Calculus Volume 3, 6.2 Line Integrals: Calculate a scalar line integral along a curve.
body: OpenStax Calculus Volume 3, section "6.2 Line Integrals", prints these objectives: "Calculate a scalar line integral along a curve." "Calculate a vector line integral along an oriented curve in space." "Use a line integral to compute the work done in moving an object along a curve in a vector field." "Describe the flux and circulation of a vector field.". The section text says: "We are familiar with single-variable integrals of the form ∫ a b f ( x ) d x , where the domain of integration is an interval [ a , b ] . Such an interval can be thought of as a curve in the xy -plane, since the interval defines a line segment with endpoints ( a , 0 ) and ( b , 0 ) —in other words, a line segment located on the x -axis. Suppose we want to integrate over any curve in the plane, not just over a line segment on the x -axis. Such a task requires a new kind of integral, called a…" This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
